_comment: sample-data 4.0.0 SqlTable predicates, Serializer 1.0.1-beta config schema (docs/configuration.md SqlTable predicate fields). Home: layers/sample-data/config/sample-data-2.4.json, which Compose-Edition unions into the composed Serializer.config.json (Compose-Edition.ps1:731-741, keyed mode|name). Every predicate is Merge: the layer is kind sample-data and ships only its own TC* rows. Order is FK-safe (parents first) and is also the harvest order; the engine re-sorts SqlTable entries by sys.foreign_keys at deserialize (SerializerOrchestrator.cs:405-429) and disables constraints per table while writing (SqlTableWriter.cs:407). Underscore keys are annotations: ConfigLoader uses default System.Text.Json options (ConfigLoader.cs:18) and ignores them, and Compose-Edition skips top-level _* keys (Compose-Edition.ps1:723). No nameColumn anywhere: file names come from the PK joined with $$, which keeps the base/cross-layer filename collision checks meaningful (base.contract.json). No serviceCaches: none of the eighteen DwCacheServiceRegistry names is verified for these tables; the host restart the layer already requires covers the caches. The two loose scripts the layer also ships (merge/_sql/demo-clock.sql, merge/_sql/email-stats.sql) are declared in layer.json sql[] and carry no predicate.

predicates.name: sample-data AccessUser
predicates._why: Merge: a re-deserialize must never reset a persona or the password UserSetPassword set. The identity key is written with IDENTITY_INSERT (SqlTableWriter.cs:45-64), so 100100..100103 survive. Password and runtime login columns are excluded; AccessUserPasswordSalt is deliberately absent because the column does not exist on DW 10.28.10 and a missing column fails config load.

predicates.name: sample-data AccessUserGroupRelation
predicates._why: Merge: additive membership into the layer's account 100100 and the base-contract groups 1325/1292/1270.

predicates.name: sample-data AccessUserSecondaryRelation
predicates._why: Merge: the one impersonation grant the layer ships, the base-contract CSR group 1292 over the layer's account group 100100 (Foundry #1261). The column direction is DW's: UserId is the impersonator, SecondaryUserId the account being impersonated. Additive, so a consumer's own grants survive a re-deserialize.

predicates.name: sample-data EcomShops
predicates._why: Merge, never Replace: EcomShops is base-owned replaceWholeTable (base.contract.json baseOwnedTables), and the base's Replace runs first and writes SHOP1 alone. This layer adds ONE row beside it, the ShopType 4 DataStructure shop that owns the data-model tree - the same shape as this layer's EcomShopGroupRelation predicate. ShopAutoId 100130 is written verbatim with IDENTITY_INSERT. The shop name is what names the workspace index field: DW derives DATAMODEL_<ShopName with spaces as underscores>, so 'Truvio PIM' gives DATAMODEL_Truvio_PIM, which DynamicStructureLevels 100171 and the Products.index SkipDataModels=False build both depend on. Rename the shop and that field name moves with it.

predicates.name: sample-data EcomShopLanguageRelation
predicates._why: Merge, never Replace: base-owned replaceWholeTable, same rule as EcomShops above. EVERY shop needs a language relation - without one DW renders the shop as a nameless node in the Data models tree - so the PIM shop carries its own ENU row at the reserved identity 100131.

predicates.name: sample-data EcomCompletionRules
predicates._why: Merge by identity id, keyed on the layer's reserved range 100160..100163 so a consumer's own rules are never touched. One rule per data model, naming its seven category fields in the AUTHORING system-name form ProductCategory|<category>|<field> (the index-side form is CustomField_<name> and matches nothing here). Ordered before EcomGroups because EcomGroups.GroupCompletionRules carries the rule id as a string - there is no FK, but a host restart reloads CompletionRuleService and ProductCategoryService together and the rule should exist when the group referencing it does.

predicates.name: sample-data EcomGroups
predicates._why: Merge: sample-data rows under the layer's own prefixes. TCGRP-* is the browsable storefront catalogue (4 top groups + 12 subgroups); TCDM-* is the PIM tree under the TCSHOP-PIM DataStructure shop - one GroupType 1 folder and four GroupType 2 data models, each with its ProductCategoryId and its own completion rule. 21 rows.

predicates.name: sample-data EcomShopGroupRelation
predicates._why: Merge, never Replace: the table is base-owned replaceWholeTable (base.contract.json); this layer only adds its own rows, as feature-reordering-pricing already does. 16 TCGRP-*$$SHOP1 rows bind the storefront catalogue to the commerce shop and 5 TCDM-*$$TCSHOP-PIM rows bind the PIM tree to the DataStructure shop. DW resolves a group to its shop through THIS table and does not walk the parent chain, so every group carries a row, folder and subgroups included.

predicates.name: sample-data EcomGroupRelations
predicates._why: Merge: sample-data rows. 12 storefront subgroup-to-top-group rows plus 4 data-model-to-folder rows under TCDM-TRUVIO-COMMERCE.

predicates.name: sample-data EcomGroupProductRelation

The predicate is keyed on the PRODUCT id, so it already fences the 61 TCDM-* data-model relations 5.0.0 adds beside the 122 TCGRP-* catalogue rows - no widening was needed. A master's data-model relation is IsPrimary false: its primary home stays its catalogue subgroup.

predicates.name: sample-data EcomProductField
predicates._why: Merge: the six STANDARD product fields DW 10.28 keeps master-only by default (variantEditing=false) - ProductNumber, ProductPrice, ProductStock, ProductShortDescription, ProductMetaTitle, ProductMetaDescription. The layer ships 36 variant rows carrying their own number, price and stock, so a master save with variant editing OFF copies the master's values onto every variant (Foundry #1253, arm B). DW 10.28 stores the per-field setting as an EcomProductField ROW (ProductFieldAllowChangesAcrossVariants; ProductFieldIsStandard = 1 marks a settings row for a standard field), NOT in GlobalSettings.Ecom.config - the /Ecom/ProductLanguageControl/Variant/* nodes are the pre-migration store and DW carries a MigrationToDatabaseDone flag beside them. Measured on foundry.mydwsite4.com 2026-09-14: the table is EMPTY on a stock Swift 2.4 host and Admin API ProductAttributeSettingsSave CREATES one row per field. PKs are TCFIELD-namespaced (base.contract.json idRules) so the layer never collides with the FIELDnnn ids the EcomNumbers 'FIELD' counter mints, and the identities are in the layer's reserved range at/above the 100000 floor.

predicates.name: sample-data EcomProductCategoryField
predicates._why: Merge: sample-data rows - the 28 concrete tc_* fields plus their 28 reference_category mirrors. reference_category is DW's hidden CategoryType 2 template category: without a mirror row per concrete field the admin completeness and rule screens resolve no field and render EMPTY while every API read answers correctly. The mirror half of the predicate is fenced to FieldId LIKE 'tc%' so it can never reach a mirror row another solution's fields put there; the reference_category PARENT row is base-owned.

predicates.name: sample-data EcomProductCategoryFieldTranslation
predicates._why: Merge: sample-data rows - 28 concrete ENU labels plus the 28 reference_category mirrors, the fourth row of the four-rows-per-field reference_category pattern. Same FieldId fence as the field predicate above.

predicates.name: sample-data EcomProductCategoryFieldValue

The id keeps its PACK- prefix because a re-key would leave the old row on every host already delivered; the key is fenced by this predicate, not by the prefix.

predicates.name: sample-data EcomCustomerFavoriteLists
predicates._why: Merge by identity id at the reserved 100401..100402: the buyer persona 100101's two favourite lists, which the Swift 2.4 dashboard Favorites widget lists. Favourites have no Delivery API route for adding a product, so the rows are data.

predicates.name: sample-data EcomCustomerFavoriteProducts
predicates._why: Merge on the natural primary key (FavoriteListId, ProductId, ProductVariantId); CustomerFavoriteProductAutoId is an identity outside the key, so the host allocates it.

predicates.name: sample-data DynamicStructures
predicates._why: Merge, matched on keyColumns DynamicStructureUniqueId (Foundry #1305, Serializer #21, engine floor 1.0.6-beta). The one Dynamic Workspace the layer ships. DynamicStructureQueryId is the Id GUID of repositories/TruvioCommerce/PimWorkspace.query, which this layer also ships; DynamicStructureUniqueId is the fixed GUID the level rows join on, a NOT NULL uniqueidentifier, which makes it the natural key. DynamicStructures has NO PRIMARY KEY on DW 10.28 (a heap: sys.indexes carries only the HEAP row, no unique index). Serializer 1.0.2-beta wrote a heap as DELETE FROM plus insert-all in every mode, so gate run 20260919-153644 on foundry.mydwsite4.com deleted the host's three baseline workspaces (ids 1, 3, 4) and orphaned their seven DynamicStructureLevels rows. 1.0.3-beta resolves a match key instead (primary key, then this keyColumns, then a unique index, then all columns), upserts, and a Merge never deletes; the run log reports a Deleted count the Foundry pim-structure leg asserts is 0. Declared rather than left to inference because the identity column is never a key and the all-columns fallback would insert a duplicate the moment the title changes. Consequence: the identity is NOT written (no IDENTITY_INSERT on a heap), so on a host that has no row with this UniqueId the target assigns DynamicStructureId; on a host delivered before, the existing row keeps its id. Nothing joins on the int id: levels join on the UniqueId. From 1.0.5-beta the engine logs the declared key as an info line; 1.0.3-beta and 1.0.4-beta logged a WARNING that fails a strict-mode API deserialize (Serializer #30). This is the only heap table the layer writes; check _meta.yml keyColumns against sys.indexes before adding another.

predicates.name: sample-data DynamicStructureLevels
predicates._why: Merge by identity id at the layer's reserved 100171..100172. Two levels: DATAMODEL_Truvio_PIM then GroupNames. DynamicStructureLevelStructureId is the DynamicStructures UniqueId GUID stored as nvarchar, not the int id. Both level sources are NON-ANALYSED keyword fields, which is the whole correctness question for a workspace level: an analysed free-text field enumerates lower-cased Lucene term fragments and a numeric field enumerates nodes that open onto zero rows, and neither errors.
